title: Student identity is directly disclosed by submitted identifiers
description: The student, as source, sends a student identifier together with the assignment submission. This directly reveals the student's identity to the receiving system as part of the act of sharing.
assumptions: The student ID is unique to an individual student and can identify them within the institution.
uncertainty_note: Tree node id is based on best judgement because the retrieved context gives applicable threat types but not detailed node definitions.

title: Assignment submissions can be linked across courses or over time in transit metadata
description: The flow contains student ID, course, and submission timestamp. Together these attributes can enable linking multiple submissions to the same student across courses or over time, even aside from the file contents.
assumptions: The transmitted metadata is observable or retained in transit logs, traces, or intermediary components.
uncertainty_note: Exact threat-tree node may differ depending on the local LINDDUN Pro taxonomy version.

title: Student identity may be exposed in transit
description: The data flow carries a student ID and likely identifying content in the assignment file. If the transmission channel or intermediaries expose payload or metadata, the student's identity can be learned from the flow.
assumptions: Transport protection may be absent, weak, terminated at intermediaries, or logs may capture identifying fields.
uncertainty_note: Applies if transport or intermediary handling exposes the data; if end-to-end protected and minimally logged, likelihood would be lower.

title: Submission behavior can be detected from network-visible metadata
description: Even if payload contents are protected, the existence, timing, size, and destination of the submission flow can reveal that a student is logging in and submitting coursework at a particular time.
assumptions: An observer can access network metadata, reverse-proxy logs, or similar telemetry.
uncertainty_note: Tree node id is approximate; the threat is grounded in detectability via communication metadata.

title: Portal can link submissions to the same student across contexts
description: On receipt, the Grades Portal Web App can correlate student ID, course, timestamps, login context, and assignment files to link multiple actions and submissions belonging to the same student across time and possibly across courses.
assumptions: The portal stores or processes these fields together and has access to historical submissions or account activity.

title: Portal learns the student's identity and potentially personal information in the assignment
description: The destination receives the student ID and assignment file, which may contain the student's name or other personal information. This enables identification of the student and possibly disclosure of additional personal details contained in the work.
assumptions: Assignment files may embed names, authorship metadata, comments, or other personal content.

title: Portal can observe and infer submission activity patterns
description: By receiving the submission timestamp, course, and file, the portal can detect when the student logs in and submits work, enabling inference about study habits, deadlines, lateness, or engagement.
assumptions: The portal records receipt times and associates them with the student's account.

title: Submission may be processed beyond the student's expectations or without sufficient transparency
description: The portal may use the submitted assignment and associated identifiers for purposes beyond accepting the assignment, such as plagiarism detection, analytics, retention, or sharing with other institutional systems, without sufficiently clear notice or choice at the point of submission.
assumptions: Secondary uses, extended retention, or onward sharing are possible and not fully explained to the student during submission.
uncertainty_note: This is a plausible non-compliance threat at the destination, but confirmation depends on the actual notices, legal basis, and institutional policies.

title: Portal shares more personal data than strictly necessary with grading service
description: The portal forwards student id, course, file reference, and requesting role to the assignment & grading service. If all of these attributes are not strictly required for each request type, the source process causes avoidable disclosure of personal data across an internal boundary, contrary to data minimization.
assumptions: Assumes some routed operations could be fulfilled with fewer attributes, or with pseudonymous/internal references instead of direct student identifiers.
uncertainty_note: Tree node citation is based on best judgement because the retrieved context gives Dd methodology but not the exact Dd subtree node.

title: Data flow contains direct identifier for the student
description: The transmitted payload includes student id, which is a unique reference to the data subject. Anyone able to observe or access this flow can identify which student's submission or grading request is being processed.

title: Assignment service processes identified student data
description: The destination service receives and processes identified data about the student when handling submission and grading requests. Processing can therefore be tied directly to a specific individual rather than an anonymous or pseudonymous subject.
assumptions: Assumes the student id is retained or used by the service as part of request handling rather than immediately transformed into a less identifying token.

title: Submission and grading requests may be linkable across courses or actions
description: Repeated transmission of the same student id together with course and role over this flow can enable correlation of multiple requests, linking a student's submissions and grading-related interactions across time or contexts.
assumptions: Assumes observers or receiving-side logs can correlate repeated occurrences of the same identifiers and contextual attributes.
uncertainty_note: Exact L subtree node is selected by best judgement; retrieved context did not include a specific linkability node.

title: Flow reveals educational context and role metadata in transit
description: Beyond the file reference itself, the combination of student id, course, and requesting role discloses educational context and participation metadata. If any intermediary, logger, or unauthorized observer can access the flow, this creates avoidable disclosure of personal data and contextual information.
assumptions: Assumes the flow or associated transport/logging path is observable by components or personnel not needing all transmitted fields.
uncertainty_note: Tree node citation is approximate because the retrieved context did not provide the exact Dd subtree.

title: Excessive personal data stored with submission
description: The grading service stores the assignment file together with student id, course, and submission time. If all of these attributes are not strictly necessary for grading or later academic administration, the act of sending them to persistent storage creates avoidable disclosure through over-collection and over-storage of personal data.
assumptions: Assumes at least some of the stored attributes could be reduced, pseudonymised, or separated without breaking the intended purpose.
uncertainty_note: Tree node chosen as best-fit for explicit/minimisation-related disclosure; exact node label may vary by LINDDUN Pro version.

title: Submission metadata enables linkage of student activity
description: The data flow carries student id, course, and submission time alongside the assignment file. Together these fields can link this submission to other records about the same student across courses, deadlines, and platform events, enabling correlation of behaviour beyond the immediate grading purpose.
assumptions: Assumes the same student identifier or correlated metadata is used elsewhere in the system.
uncertainty_note: Exact threat-tree node may differ across catalog versions; linkage via stable identifiers and timestamps is the core concern.

title: Student identity is directly exposed in transit to storage
description: Because the flow includes a student id with the submission, the data in transit directly identifies the submitting student to any component or observer with access to the flow, rather than using a less identifying token.
assumptions: Assumes the student id is directly identifying within the system context.
uncertainty_note: Applies even on an internal flow if multiple components, logs, or operators can observe the transfer.

title: Persistent storage may disclose more personal data than necessary
description: On receipt, the assignment store persists the assignment content and associated identifiers/timestamps. Retaining these data together in a datastore can create avoidable disclosure risk if the store keeps them longer than needed, stores them in unnecessarily identifiable form, or makes them broadly accessible for secondary purposes.
assumptions: Assumes the datastore retains and exposes stored records beyond the minimum necessary operational scope.
uncertainty_note: Best-fit node for disclosure caused by storage/retention at destination; exact node id may vary.

title: Storage of submissions may enable use beyond the student's expectations
description: Students may expect their submission to be used for grading, but storing the full file with identity, course, and timestamp in the assignment store can enable additional uses such as analytics, plagiarism corpus building, training datasets, or long-term profiling unless those uses are clearly specified and constrained.
assumptions: Assumes purposes beyond immediate grading are technically possible and not fully constrained by policy and design.
uncertainty_note: This is a purpose-limitation/use concern; exact tree node citation is approximate.

title: Students may lack awareness or control over stored submission metadata
description: If the assignment store retains student id, course, submission time, and file content without transparent notice, configurable retention, or mechanisms to exercise privacy rights, the destination processing can undermine compliance with transparency, minimisation, retention, or rights obligations.
assumptions: Assumes relevant notice, retention controls, or rights-handling mechanisms are absent or insufficient.
uncertainty_note: Compliance impact depends on jurisdiction and actual controls; node id is best-effort.

title: Teacher submits identified login/request data
description: The teacher's login and queue request inherently contain identified data, such as account credentials, session identifiers, or an authenticated account reference tied to a specific teacher. By sending this data to the portal, the teacher becomes identifiable to the receiving system.
assumptions: Assumes the login/request includes a username, email address, employee identifier, or equivalent account-bound credential.

title: Request metadata can link teacher activity across sessions
description: Even if payload contents are minimized, metadata on this flow such as source IP address, device/browser fingerprint, timing, course-selection patterns, and repeated access to the review queue can allow linking multiple requests to the same teacher over time.
assumptions: Assumes normal web/network metadata is observable or retained along the communication path or by supporting infrastructure.
uncertainty_note: Tree node chosen by best judgement; retrieved context did not provide a more specific linkability node.

title: Teacher identity may be exposed in transit via request contents or metadata
description: Data in transit may identify the teacher directly through credentials, account identifiers, session tokens, or indirectly through network metadata associated with the request. This creates an identifying threat on the flow itself.
assumptions: Assumes the request carries account-bound identifiers or that transport metadata can be associated with a specific teacher.

title: Portal can detect the teacher's intent to review submissions
description: By receiving the login and queue request, the portal learns that this specific teacher is active and intends to review submissions for particular courses at a particular time. This reveals behavioral information about the teacher's work activity.
assumptions: Assumes the request is associated with one or more courses or review actions rather than being a generic unauthenticated page load.
uncertainty_note: Specific detectability node selected by best judgement because the retrieved context did not include detectability tree details.

title: Portal may process teacher request data beyond the teacher's expectations
description: The web app may use the teacher's login and queue-request data for secondary purposes, such as analytics, performance monitoring, profiling of staff activity, or retention in logs, without the teacher fully understanding these uses.
assumptions: Assumes the system performs logging, analytics, or operational monitoring beyond the strictly necessary authentication and queue retrieval functions.
uncertainty_note: Specific unawareness node selected by best judgement because the retrieved context did not include unawareness tree details.

title: Teacher may lack meaningful choice or consent over collection of login/request telemetry
description: To access the grading queue, the teacher may have no practical option but to provide identifying login data and generate request telemetry, while any additional collection or secondary processing may not be optional or separately consented to.
assumptions: Assumes employment context where use of the portal is mandatory and optionality over non-essential telemetry or secondary processing is limited.
uncertainty_note: Specific non-compliance/consent node selected by best judgement because the retrieved context did not include non-compliance tree details.

title: Portal may disclose more student submission data than necessary to the teacher
description: The web app intentionally shares student names, work content, and submission times with the teacher. A privacy threat exists if the portal exposes fields, historical submissions, or timing details beyond what is necessary for the teacher's legitimate task, violating data minimization.
assumptions: Assumes the teacher does not always need all displayed attributes or all submissions visible in one view.
uncertainty_note: Tree-node id is best-effort based on LINDDUN Pro data-disclosure/minimization structure; exact subnode may differ by catalog version.

title: Teacher may further disclose or retain student submissions beyond the intended purpose
description: Once received, the teacher can view and potentially copy, export, screenshot, or otherwise redistribute student names, work content, and submission times. This creates a privacy threat if the recipient processes or shares the data beyond the educational purpose for which the portal disclosed it.
assumptions: Assumes the teacher interface or surrounding environment permits onward sharing, local storage, or secondary use.
uncertainty_note: Exact Dd subtree citation is approximate; threat applicability is strong but node numbering may vary.

title: Submission metadata in transit can identify specific students
description: The flow contains direct identifiers such as student names and associated submission details. If the transmission is observable or insufficiently protected, the data in transit can identify individual students.
assumptions: Assumes there is some opportunity for interception or observation of the flow, e.g. weak transport protection, shared devices, or exposed browser/network artifacts.
uncertainty_note: Identification clearly applies in substance, but the exact tree-node id is best-effort.

title: Submission records and timestamps enable linking of student activity across contexts
description: Names combined with work content and submission times can allow correlation of a student's activity across assignments, classes, or other systems, especially if similar identifiers and timestamps are reused. The flow itself therefore carries linkable data.
assumptions: Assumes the teacher or an observer can correlate these attributes with other records or contexts.
uncertainty_note: Linkability is plausible from the described attributes; exact node numbering is approximate.

title: Observed submission details may reveal sensitive aspects of a student
description: Work content and submission timing can reveal personal characteristics or circumstances, such as learning difficulties, health-related absences, religious observance patterns, or behavioral traits. Even if not explicitly stated, these attributes may be inferred from the transmitted data.
assumptions: Assumes the content or timing patterns are sufficiently distinctive to support such inferences.
uncertainty_note: Detectability/inference risk depends on the actual content and context; exact tree-node id is approximate.

title: Teacher can later deny having submitted or authored a specific grade/feedback entry
description: Because the teacher is the source of the grade, feedback text, student id, and grader id, insufficient binding of the submission to the teacher's authenticated session or lack of trustworthy submission evidence could allow the teacher to repudiate having entered or changed a student's grade or written feedback.
assumptions: Applies if the portal does not create tamper-evident audit records or strong proof of submission tied to the teacher identity and time.
uncertainty_note: Tree-node id is based on best judgement; exact LINDDUN Pro subnode may differ.

title: Grade submission flow can identify both student and teacher in transit
description: The transmitted payload contains student id and grader id, and may also include assignment context, grade, and free-text feedback. Anyone able to observe the flow or its metadata could identify the involved student and teacher.
assumptions: Applies especially if transport protection is weak, terminated in an untrusted intermediary, or metadata is exposed beyond intended recipients.
uncertainty_note: Exact subnode may vary depending on the project's threat-tree granularity.

title: Repeated grade submissions can be linked to the same teacher or student
description: Across multiple submissions, stable identifiers such as student id and grader id allow records on this flow to be linked together, revealing grading patterns, teacher workload, or a student's assessment history.
assumptions: Applies when identifiers remain stable across transactions and observers or intermediaries can correlate multiple flow instances.
uncertainty_note: Linkability may also arise from metadata such as account/session identifiers, timestamps, or network identifiers.

title: Sensitive academic-performance data may be disclosed while in transit
description: The flow carries confidential educational data: a student's grade, written feedback, and associated identifiers. Interception, logging, or unintended exposure of this traffic could disclose the student's performance and the teacher's evaluative comments to unauthorized parties.
assumptions: Applies if encryption, endpoint validation, or intermediary handling are insufficient, or if traffic is logged inappropriately.
uncertainty_note: Exact node selection is approximate; this is a generic disclosure-in-transit threat.

title: Portal may disclose grades or feedback beyond authorized educational recipients
description: Once the Grades Portal Web App receives the submission, its processing or storage of grade, feedback text, student id, and grader id could expose this educational record to unauthorized staff, other students, or external systems through overly broad access, insecure storage, or excessive onward sharing.
assumptions: Applies if role-based access control, storage protection, or downstream sharing controls are inadequate.
uncertainty_note: Destination-side disclosure is strongly plausible, but exact subnode is based on best judgement.

title: Portal may use submitted grades and feedback for secondary purposes without the data subjects' awareness
description: The web app could reuse grade and feedback submissions for analytics, staff performance monitoring, model training, or other secondary processing not expected by the teacher or student, creating an unawareness threat at the destination.
assumptions: Applies if privacy notices are incomplete or if secondary uses are not clearly communicated to teachers and students.
uncertainty_note: This depends on organizational practices not explicit in the flow description.

title: Portal processing of student grades and feedback may lack a valid legal basis or exceed educational necessity
description: The destination system receives identifiable educational records and teacher-authored feedback. If the portal stores or further processes these data without an appropriate legal basis, beyond stated educational purposes, or longer than necessary, the processing may be non-compliant with applicable privacy obligations.
assumptions: Applies depending on jurisdiction, institutional policy, retention rules, and whether processing purposes are properly defined and limited.
uncertainty_note: Compliance assessment is jurisdiction-specific; exact node id is approximate.

title: Grade record content enables linkage across courses and assessments
description: When the Assignment & Grading Service writes records containing student id, course, grade, feedback, grader id, and timestamp, the combination of stable student and grader identifiers with course and time data can link multiple grading events to the same student and grader over time.
assumptions: Student id and grader id are persistent identifiers reused across records.
uncertainty_note: Tree-node id is based on best judgement because the retrieved context gives applicable threat types but not detailed node mappings.

title: Direct identification of student and grader in stored grade records
description: The grading service writes directly identifying attributes, notably student id and grader id, into the database. This makes the data subject and associated staff member identifiable from the record.
assumptions: Identifiers can be resolved to real individuals by authorized or unauthorized recipients with access to the database.
uncertainty_note: Detailed threat-tree node id is approximate.

title: Disclosure of sensitive academic performance data in transit
description: The flow carries grade records including grades and qualitative feedback. If the transmission channel is observable or insufficiently protected, sensitive academic performance information and associated identifiers may be exposed during transfer to the database.
assumptions: Transport protections may be absent, weak, or bypassed in some deployment scenarios.
uncertainty_note: Applies if data in transit is not adequately protected; if strong authenticated encryption is enforced end-to-end, likelihood would be lower.

title: Stored grade records may be disclosed beyond intended educational purposes
description: Once received, the Grade Records Database stores highly sensitive educational records, feedback, grader identity, and timestamps. Inadequate access control, excessive retention, broad internal querying, or secondary use could disclose these records to parties not entitled to see them.
assumptions: The database may be queried by multiple roles or integrated with other systems.
uncertainty_note: Detailed node id is approximate.

title: Database storage enables inference of student performance patterns
description: Aggregated grade records over time can allow inference of a student's academic strengths, weaknesses, progression, risk status, or special circumstances. Feedback text and timestamps may further reveal behavioral or contextual details not explicitly stated.
assumptions: Historical records are retained and can be analyzed together.
uncertainty_note: Detailed node id is approximate.

title: Repurposing grade records for incompatible secondary uses
description: The destination database may enable later use of grade records, feedback, grader identifiers, and timestamps for purposes beyond grading and academic recordkeeping, such as staff performance monitoring, student profiling, analytics, or disciplinary decisions, without compatibility assessment or additional safeguards.
assumptions: Data in DS2 may be accessible for analytics, reporting, or administrative reuse.
uncertainty_note: This is a destination-side misuse risk contingent on governance and access practices.

title: Storage of detailed grading data may exceed necessity or retention limits
description: Persisting full feedback, precise timestamps, grader id, and stable student identifiers for every grading event may collect or retain more personal data than necessary for the immediate purpose, especially if all fields are kept indefinitely or copied into broad-access stores.
assumptions: No minimization, field-level necessity review, or retention limits are enforced.
uncertainty_note: Detailed node id is approximate.

title: Insufficient evidence of who wrote or altered grade records
description: If the database does not preserve trustworthy provenance for writes from the grading service, the institution may be unable to prove which grader or service action created or modified a grade record, enabling repudiation of grading actions and undermining accountability to data subjects.
assumptions: Audit trails, integrity protection, or attribution mechanisms may be incomplete.
uncertainty_note: Included because the flow explicitly carries grader id and timestamp, suggesting accountability matters; applicability depends on actual audit design.

title: Student submits identified request data
description: To request grades and feedback, the student typically sends identified data such as login/session identifiers or student number, causing the request to be tied to a specific person.
assumptions: Assumes the portal requires authenticated or otherwise identifiable requests to retrieve personal grades.

title: Request metadata can link repeated grade-access events
description: Metadata on the request flow, such as stable account identifiers, IP address, device/browser fingerprints, timestamps, and repeated access patterns, can allow linking multiple grade-access requests to the same student over time.
assumptions: Assumes network, application, or intermediary logs observe persistent identifiers or quasi-identifiers on this flow.
uncertainty_note: Threat-tree node id is best-effort because the retrieved context did not include specific linkability subnodes.

title: Request flow contains identifying information
description: Data in transit may directly identify the student through usernames, student IDs, session tokens bound to identity, or other account identifiers included with the request.
assumptions: Assumes the request carries direct identifiers or tokens readily attributable to the student.

title: Portal can observe the student's interest in specific academic records
description: By receiving the request, the web app learns that this student is accessing grades and feedback at a particular time, which may reveal behavior or concerns beyond the minimum needed to serve the request if logged or profiled.
assumptions: Assumes the portal logs or analyzes access events rather than using them only ephemerally to fulfill the request.
uncertainty_note: Tree-node id is approximate because the retrieved context did not include detectability/disclosure subnodes.

title: Portal may process the request without sufficient transparency or consent basis
description: If the grades portal uses the student's request data for secondary purposes such as analytics, profiling, or retention beyond servicing the request, the collection and processing may exceed the student's expectations or consent/legal basis.
assumptions: Assumes possible secondary use, retention, or analytics on request data beyond strictly necessary service delivery.
uncertainty_note: This applies only if the portal uses request data beyond what is necessary to provide the grades service; exact node id is best-effort.

title: Portal may disclose grades and feedback to the wrong student account
description: The web app sends highly personal academic records and teacher feedback to an external entity. If session handling, account binding, or authorization checks are flawed, P1 could disclose one student's grades and feedback to another student.
assumptions: Assumes the portal relies on authentication/session state to determine which student's records to display.
uncertainty_note: Tree-node id is best-effort based on general LINDDUN disclosure taxonomy; exact subnode may differ in the project's threat tree version.

title: Grades and feedback could be exposed in transit
description: The data flow carries sensitive educational information from the portal to the student. If transport protection is absent, weak, or downgraded, an eavesdropper could read grades and teacher feedback while in transit.
assumptions: Assumes network transport or client-side delivery path could be observed by an attacker if not properly protected end-to-end.
uncertainty_note: Tree-node id is approximate; the core issue is disclosure of content during transmission.

title: Traffic metadata may reveal when a student checks grades
description: Even if content is encrypted, metadata about this flow may reveal that a particular student is accessing the grades portal at a specific time, enabling linkage between the student's identity and grade-checking events or academic milestones.
assumptions: Assumes observers can see communication endpoints, timing, or frequency metadata.
uncertainty_note: Exact LINDDUN subnode may vary; this is a metadata-based linkability threat.

title: Displaying grades on the student's device may enable shoulder-surfing or local disclosure
description: Once received, the student's device/browser displays grades and feedback. Other people near the student or with access to the device may observe the information, causing unwanted detectability/disclosure of the student's academic performance.
assumptions: Assumes the destination context includes display on a potentially shared or observable device.
uncertainty_note: This is a destination-side privacy risk tied to receipt/display; classification between Detectability and Disclosure may vary by modeling convention.

title: Student may be unaware of onward exposure risks after viewing feedback
description: The student may not be adequately informed that grades and teacher feedback can remain visible in browser history, screenshots, notifications, cached pages, or shared devices, limiting informed control over subsequent exposure.
assumptions: Assumes the portal does not clearly communicate client-side privacy implications or provide privacy-preserving viewing controls.
uncertainty_note: Non-compliance depends on applicable transparency/notice obligations and portal design details, which are not provided.

title: Parent submits identified account credentials and child-linked request
description: The parent initiates the flow by providing login/request data that is directly tied to an identified parent account and implicitly to a specific child account. This sharing enables identification of both the parent and the associated student within the service context.
assumptions: Assumes the login/request contains account identifiers, credentials, session identifiers, or other data that uniquely maps the parent to a child record.

title: Linkability of parent and child through request metadata in transit
description: The flow itself can reveal that a particular parent account is linked to a particular child account or student record. Even if payload contents are protected, traffic metadata, identifiers, cookies, URLs, or request parameters may allow linking repeated requests to the same family relationship.
assumptions: Assumes the request carries stable identifiers or observable metadata that can correlate the parent with the child/account relationship.
uncertainty_note: Tree node chosen by best judgement; retrieved context did not include a more specific linkability node.

title: Identification via account and session data in transit
description: Data sent on this flow may contain usernames, email addresses, parent account IDs, child/student IDs, or session tokens that identify the parent and/or child if exposed or insufficiently minimized in transit-visible elements such as headers, URLs, or metadata.
assumptions: Assumes identifiers are present in the request or its metadata.

title: Portal learns sensitive educational interest from the parent's request
description: By receiving and processing the request for a child's grades, the portal can infer private information about the family's educational relationship and the parent's interest in a specific student's academic performance. This goes beyond mere authentication and reveals a sensitive purpose of use.
assumptions: Assumes the request semantics clearly indicate that the parent is accessing grade information for a linked child.
uncertainty_note: Specific threat-tree citation is based on best judgement because the retrieved context did not include disclosure nodes.

title: Unawareness if the portal does not clearly explain parent-child account linkage processing
description: When the portal receives this request, the parent may be unaware of how the system uses, stores, or audits the linkage between the parent account and the child account, including what grade-access events are recorded and who can see them.
assumptions: Assumes privacy notices or just-in-time explanations may be absent or insufficient.
uncertainty_note: Specific tree node chosen by best judgement; retrieved context did not include unawareness nodes.

title: Non-compliance risk from processing child grade data via parent linkage without proper legal basis or minimization
description: The destination process may process parent and child educational data in a way that violates privacy obligations if it does not enforce appropriate authorization, purpose limitation, data minimization, retention, or transparency for parent access to student records.
assumptions: Assumes applicable education/privacy regulation or policy governs parental access to student data.
uncertainty_note: Specific tree node chosen by best judgement; retrieved context did not include non-compliance nodes.

title: Portal discloses excessive educational records to the parent
description: The web app may share more of the child's educational record than is necessary for the parent's purpose, such as full submission history, detailed teacher feedback, or grades from contexts the parent should not access. The source process causes the threat by deciding what data to present.
assumptions: Assumes parental access should be limited by role, custody, student age, consent, or least-privilege rules rather than unrestricted access to all historical records.
uncertainty_note: Tree-node id is based on best judgement for disclosure/excessive sharing because the retrieved context did not include detailed threat-tree nodes.

title: Portal output can identify the child through named academic records
description: Displaying grades, feedback, and submission history to the parent directly identifies the child and ties the child to specific educational performance data. If the portal session is accessed by the wrong person, the source process has enabled identification of the student from the shared content.
assumptions: Assumes the portal view contains the child's name, class, identifiers, or otherwise uniquely identifying academic context.
uncertainty_note: Identification is inherent to this flow, but whether it is a privacy threat depends on whether the recipient is always the correct authenticated parent.

title: Academic records can be linked across time and subjects in the parent view
description: By presenting grades, teacher feedback, and submission history together, the portal enables the parent account to link multiple events, subjects, and time periods into a detailed profile of the child's academic behavior and performance.
assumptions: Assumes the portal aggregates records across courses or time rather than showing only a single isolated item.
uncertainty_note: This may be expected functionality, but it still represents a linkability risk if broader aggregation than necessary is exposed.

title: Data in transit may reveal the child's identity and school context
description: If transport protections are weak or metadata is exposed, the flow carrying grades and feedback can reveal that a specific parent is accessing a specific child's educational records, identifying both the child and their relationship to the school.
assumptions: Assumes inadequate transport encryption, leakage via URLs, referrers, browser caches, or observable traffic metadata.
uncertainty_note: Applies mainly if the implementation exposes content or sensitive identifiers in transit or in protocol metadata.

title: Sensitive educational content may be disclosed in transit
description: Grades, teacher feedback, and submission history are sensitive student records. If the flow is intercepted, cached insecurely, or embedded in URLs or notifications, unauthorized parties could learn the child's academic performance.
assumptions: Assumes insecure transport, intermediary logging, shared-device exposure, or sensitive data placed in GET parameters or front-end resources.
uncertainty_note: Threat depends on implementation details of transport, caching, and front-end delivery.

title: Parent-side viewing may disclose the child's records to unauthorized household members
description: Once received by the parent, the displayed grades and feedback may be visible to other people using the same device, browser profile, email previews, or screenshots, causing onward disclosure at the destination.
assumptions: Assumes shared devices, unattended sessions, or lack of privacy controls on the parent side.
uncertainty_note: This is a destination-side privacy threat because it depends on how the recipient environment handles the received data.

title: Parent may receive records without valid authorization or consent basis
description: The destination may receive the child's grades and feedback even when the parent is not legally or organizationally entitled to them, for example due to custody restrictions, revoked rights, age-related confidentiality rules, or missing consent/notice conditions.
assumptions: Assumes access rights can vary by parent, student age, legal status, or school policy.
uncertainty_note: Modeled at the destination because the privacy issue materializes when this external entity receives data without a valid basis; exact legal basis depends on jurisdiction and school policy.

title: Parent may be unaware of scope and downstream use of the child's academic data
description: The recipient may not understand how much historical academic information is being provided, how long it remains accessible, or whether it can be downloaded, shared, or reused, reducing transparency around the child's data exposure.
assumptions: Assumes the portal does not clearly explain scope, retention, downloadability, or sharing implications of the displayed records.
uncertainty_note: Unawareness is somewhat atypical for a simple display flow, but can apply if the interface lacks clear privacy notices or contextual explanations.

title: Administrator may disclose excessive account and relationship data when managing users
description: The school administrator sends names, emails, roles, and parent-child relationship data to the portal. If the administrator enters or submits more personal data than necessary for the account-management task, or updates the wrong person's record, personal information is disclosed from the source side.
assumptions: The administrator can create/modify/disable accounts and parent-child links through this flow, and the submitted payload may contain multiple identifiers and relationship attributes.
uncertainty_note: Tree-node id is based on best judgement because the retrieved context did not include detailed threat-tree nodes.

title: Account-management traffic can identify individuals and their roles in transit
description: The flow carries names, emails, roles, and family-link information. If the transmission is observable, these attributes can directly identify students, parents, or staff, and reveal which administrator action concerns which person.
assumptions: The data flow may be exposed to network observers or intermediary infrastructure if transport protections are weak or metadata is logged.
uncertainty_note: Exact threat-tree node may differ in the formal LINDDUN Pro tree; selected as best-fit identification-in-transit node.

title: Relationship and role data in transit can link family members and accounts
